newsitem.title: USA: Golden Star sees Dachine results in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Golden Star sees Dachine results in Feb.

text.p: Golden Star Resources Ltd said results from laboratory tests of samples provided by ongoing diamond exploration within the Dachine permit area in French Guiana should be available in late February.

Guyanor Ressources SA, Golden Star's about 69 percent owned French subsidiary, and Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd's BHP Minerals International agreed in December 1995 to jointly explore the Dachine diamond occurrence. BHP is the project manager under the agreement.
Golden Star said sample collection from pits began in late August gathered about 207 metric tonnes of material.

A gravity jig plant began operating at the site in September and is processing excavated material to produce a heavy mineral concentrate. About 90 tonnes have been treated, and the work is expected to be completed by mid-December.
The heavy mineral concentrates will be shipped to BHP's Minerals Laboratory in Reno, Nev., for diamond recovery, Golden Star said.
Processing has been completed at Golden Star's Georgetown, Guyana, laboratory of 31 stream sediment samples from creeks draining the Dachine body, the company said.
Macrodiamonds were reported in all the samples, the largest stone measuring 2.7 milimeters in its widest dimension, it said.
